contributions.statement: If an LLM planner emits a task DAG, grow it a few nodes at a time from the evaluated results of finished nodes instead of committing the full plan from the task statement and patching it: with the same model and tools, a single upfront DAG scored no better than a long-context ReAct loop, plan-then-patch cost ~40% more tokens for less accuracy, and incremental growth scored highest.
contributions.evidence: Table 2 (Qwen3-32B, same tool stack): single upfront plan 43.7 avg vs Table 1 ReAct-109K 43.0, Fold 46.3, Flash-Searcher 47.1; Plan-then-Patch 51.2; Evaluate-then-Grow 55.9. Table 10 (BrowseComp-Plus): Plan-then-Patch 1.68M vs 1.20M tokens, 17.6 vs 11.8 nodes, off-chain share 0.40 vs 0.25. Deep-research QA, not coding; GAIA uses an LLM equivalence judge; prompt-layer ablations are single-seed (audit).

contributions.statement: In a task DAG, give each node only compact conclusions from its direct dependencies, with full upstream transcripts retrievable on demand, rather than the whole upstream history.
contributions.evidence: Table 2: removing Selective Propagation costs 12.6/10.6/8.0 points, QueryDoc 8.0/7.7/5.0, InteractionTranscript/recall 4.0/2.9/2.0 on BrowseComp-Plus/GAIA/xbench. What replaces each component in the ablation is not specified, and Summary Agent is mixed against ReAct-109K (audit), so the effect of summarization alone is not isolated.
relative_to: 2607.02807 pass only short attempt summaries to the orchestrator

reason: The within-architecture ablation separates when an LLM-generated DAG helps (evidence-conditioned incremental growth) from when it does not (upfront plan, which ties a linear loop), a boundary the KB's prior DAG-planning entries lacked; the RL results do not transfer to hosted coding agents.
